text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Logging activities have been discovered on Selangor state land which is to be gazetted for a proposed Malaysia Wetland Sanctuary. Selangor chief minister Muhammad Muhammad Taib has ordered an immediate investigation.

-- Malaysia has virtually won its bid to host a leg of the Formula One motor-racing championship in 1999. Formula One Constructors' Association chief Bernie Ecclestone said in Lisbon: "We will be in Malaysia in 1999." Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad visited the Estoril racing site in Portugal accompanied by Ecclestone.

-- Commodities and manufacturing firm Parit Perak Holdings Bhd has seen the entry of a new substantial shareholder and recent appointment of two directors. Azman Ahmad, a director at Tongkah Holdings Bhd last week declared his 31.43 percent in Parit Perak through Primal Vision Sdn Bhd.

-- Proposed basic guidelines for internal auditors at financial institutions which Bank Negara hopes to implement by Jan 1 will cover at least six critical areas -- credit operations, treasury functions, derivatives, investment in debt and equity securities, information systems, and insurance underwriting and claims.

-- Malaysia's National Security Council meeting in the middle of next month will come up with effective strategies to handle the problem of illegal immigrants in eastern Sabah state, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
-- Malaysia's second national airline Pacific Eagle, operated by AirAsia Sdn Bhd, will take to the skies on November 17, AirAsia director Tik Mustaffa said in an interview.

-- The Sabah state cabinet will deliberate this week on proposed changes to laws governing the state timber industry. The aim of the proposals is to introduce a policy to promote "multiple use" of Sabah forest resources.
